# FAQ: Constitutional AI Red Teaming with Adversarial Prompts

## What is Constitutional AI red teaming?

It is red teaming used in two places in Constitutional AI. Before training, red-team prompts supply the harmful first drafts that the critique and revision loop fixes and the prompts for AI preference labels. After training, held-out red-team prompts and fresh human red teaming test whether the model is actually safer.

## Should red-team prompts be written by people or generated by a model?

Both. People are better at inventing new attack styles, and a model can produce far more prompts across more variations. The Constitutional AI paper combined human-written prompts from earlier Anthropic red teaming with a larger set generated by few-shot prompting a pretrained model.

## How do I stop the test set from leaking into training?

Split prompts by base prompt before generating variants, and keep the held-out pool in a separate store the training pipeline cannot read. Check new training data for near duplicates of held-out prompts before each run.

## What should I do when red teaming finds a failure?

Record the transcript, the category and the attack style. Then decide whether the fix is a new or reworded principle, more training prompts in that area, or a control outside training such as input and output filtering. Add a held-out prompt for the failure so future rounds test it.

## Does a trained model still need red teaming?

Yes. Training changes the model, and new weaknesses appear, especially under jailbreak styles the training data did not include. Anthropic's own work on universal jailbreaks relied on extensive human red teaming of guarded models, and the Constitutional AI paper names robustness to red-team attacks as an open problem.

## How do I handle the harmful content red teaming produces?

Limit access to people who need it, store outputs securely, and avoid spreading harmful drafts beyond the training pipeline. The Constitutional AI paper notes that one benefit of the method is reducing how much disturbing content human red teamers and labelers must engage with, so keep that benefit by automating what you safely can.
